r.description: approximate route of Charles II's escape

r.name: Staffordshire Way (Cannock Chase South)
r.description: Staffordshire Way, part Cannock Chase - south

r.name: Silkin Way
r.description: Cycle route that follows disused railway lines and canal beds. The path was opened in 1977 by Prime Minister James Callaghan, and was named after Lord Silkin; who was a parliamentarian responsible for creating New Towns including Telford.

r.name: Parkland and Meadow Walk, Benthall Hall
r.description: This short circular walk takes you through the parkland immediately in front of Benthall Hall. This can be muddy in wet weather and winter months, so sensible walking footwear is advised.

r.name: Telford T50
r.description: The T50 Trail links parks, woods, nature reserves, and historic sites across Telford, starting and ending at Town Park. It’s easily accessible from estates and bus routes, with key points at Ironbridge, The Wrekin, Lilleshall Hill, and Granville Park.

r.name: Captain Geoffrey's Woodland Walk, Dudmaston Estate
r.description: The walk uses natural paths which can be muddy or slippery. Dogs are welcome.

r.name: Three Pools Walk, Comer Woods, Dudmaston
r.description: The walk uses natural paths which can be muddy or slippery. Dogs are welcome.

r.name: Explorer Trail, Comer Woods, Dudmaston Estate
r.description: Some steep slopes. Dogs are welcome (on and off lead areas)

r.name: White Admiral Walk, Comer Woods, Dudmaston Estate
r.description: Some steep slopes. Paths can get seasonally muddy. Dog friendly.

r.name: Morfe Walk, Comer Woods, Dudmaston Estate
r.description: All walks use natural paths which can be muddy or slippery. Dog friendly.

r.name: Woodland and Countryside Walk, Benthall Hall
r.description: This hike through native woodland takes in quarries and fossils, then opens up to reveal expansive views of north Shropshire. This can be muddy in wet weather and winter months, so sensible walking footwear is advised.

r.name: Ironbridge Walk, Benthall Hall
r.description: This can be muddy in wet weather and winter months, so sensible walking footwear is advised. This route includes stiles, lots of steps and some steep climbs. The parkland in front of Benthall Hall contains cattle at certain times of year.

r.name: George Maw Trail, Benthall Hall
r.description: This can be muddy in wet weather and winter months, so sensible walking footwear is advised. This route includes stiles, lots of steps and some steep climbs. The parkland in front of Benthall Hall contains cattle at certain times of year.
